sentences.text: This study examined how oligodendrocyte cells, which mature from simple precursors into myelin-producing cells, change shape during development, revealing that the ion channel TRPML1 controls this morphological process.

Activation of TRPML1 leads to an increase in actin filaments, a process controlled by the protein Rac1, while these physical changes are linked to brief releases of calcium from internal storage compartments within the cell's extensions.
In young mice lacking the TRPML1 gene, levels of an active form of the PAK1 protein were lower in the brain's motor area and the main connection between the two hemispheres.
